# Native media fixtures

These small, committed fixtures are generated synthetic signals, with no recordings or third-party artwork. Tests need no FFmpeg installation at runtime. Container metadata may vary when regenerated with another FFmpeg version; the checked-in bytes define the fixture.

- `tracks.mkv`: one second of 16×16 red lossless H.264 video and an 8 kHz PCM sine tone. Used to verify that selected video and audio tracks both reach frontend metadata.
- `artwork.flac`: one second of an 8 kHz FLAC sine tone, with a 2×2 PNG picture (red upper row, blue lower row) embedded as an attached picture. Used to distinguish music artwork from a selected motion-video track and to verify file changes clear artwork state.

Generate the cover with a binary PPM header `P6\n2 2\n255\n`, followed by RGB bytes for two red pixels and two blue pixels. Then encode with FFmpeg:

```text
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i color=c=red:s=16x16:r=10:d=1 -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=8000:duration=1 -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v libx264 -preset ultrafast -crf 0 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a pcm_s16le -metadata title="Foxide track metadata fixture" tracks.mkv
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=8000:duration=1 -i cover.ppm -map 0:a -map 1:v -c:a flac -sample_fmt s16 -c:v png -disposition:v attached_pic -metadata title="Foxide artwork fixture" -metadata artist="Foxide synthetic fixtures" artwork.flac
```

The two GLSL fixtures are original synthetic test code: one inverts RGB at the mpv MAIN hook; one deliberately contains invalid syntax to test recoverable compiler errors. The punctuation in the valid shader filename checks structured path-list handling.

H.264 keeps this metadata fixture compatible with Ubuntu 24.04’s mpv 0.37 demuxer. The newer FFmpeg V_FFV1 Matroska tag is not recognized there; decoder/container-version compatibility is not the behavior under test in this fixture.

Do not add a global video-frame limit to the FLAC generation command: it can finish encoding before any audio samples are written. Native acceptance requires a configured audio output and an advancing clock in addition to the embedded picture. GPU tests select null audio output explicitly; displayed pixels are still rendered through the actual shared GL texture.

ICC fixtures: srgb.icc was generated by Pillow ImageCms/Little CMS with createProfile(sRGB). linear-rgb.icc preserves the sRGB primaries and replaces shared rTRC/gTRC/bTRC data with a one-entry gamma-1 curve, updating their tag sizes. Little CMS independently maps neutral RGB 128 to 55 through this target profile. gray.flac reuses the real sine audio and embeds a uniform RGB-128 PNG. These are synthetic transform references, not profiles measured from a monitor. The GPU test must change and restore the final rendered pixels; accepting an option alone is insufficient.
